==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-due to.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Preposition===
{{en-head|prep}}

# [[caused|Caused]] by; [[result]]ing from; [[because of]].
#: {{ux|en|Rising unemployment '''due to''' the economic downturn is spreading.}}
#: {{ux|en|The carrier will be held financially responsible for any damage '''due to''' reckless handling.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Due to''' the rising cost of ingredients, the company decided to change the recipe. [disjunctive use, [[due to#Usage notes|sometimes proscribed]]]}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|year=1908|passage=The accident was '''due to''' the breaking of one of the blades of the propeller on the left side.|title=[[S:Fatal fall of Wright airship|Fatal fall of Wright airship]]}}
# {{&lit|en}}
#: {{ux|en|The steamship was '''due to''' arrive in the Port of New York tomorrow.}}
#: {{ux|en|Our deep gratitude is '''due to''' all those who have helped.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics}} (of a proof) from, [[written]] by
#: {{ux|en|The proof we provide is a nice indirect proof '''due to''' Euclid.}}

====Usage notes====
* Although usage of "due to" as a [[disjunct#English:_linguistics|disjunctive]] preposition is now common, some speakers will object and recommend {{m|en|because of}}, {{m|en|on account of}}, {{m|en||as a result of}} or {{m|en|owing to}} instead, reserving {{m|en|due}} for use as an adjective only. Reliable sources (such as Oxford, M-W, AHDictionary, etc.) acknowledge this debate, then conclude that more recently this usage of "due to" is widely, although perhaps not entirely, acceptable. Compare also the disjunctive use of ''[[based on#Preposition|based on]]''. [https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=due+to]
* The conjunction {{m|en||due to the fact that}}, frequently encountered in business and politics, is generally rejected by style experts as being an unnecessarily wordy synonym of {{m|en|because}}.

====Synonyms====
* caused by, as a [[consequence]] of, as a [[result]] of, [[because of]], [[thanks to]], [[on account of]]
